result:
I changed nothing this hour. Everything is running and CPU is the limit, so more concurrency would only add to the throttling.

- **CPU:** load is 32.9 on a 32-core quota. A 10 s sample showed 31 cores in use and 81 of 100 periods throttled.
- **Memory:** the cgroup shows 136.5 / 137.4 GB, but only 23.0 GB is program memory; 112 GB is reclaimable file cache. No processes have been killed for running out of memory.
- **GPUs:**
  - **Mine:** GPU0 is at 34 % and GPU3 at 84 %. GPUs 1, 2 and 4 are at 0 % because the runs on them spend most of their time on the CPU.
  - **Other users:** weimin2 is on GPU0 and GPU2, another user on GPU3, and thlin fills GPUs 5 and 6.
- **Work:** 8 FEBio runs (48 threads), all with logs written in the last 3 s.
  - 3 cycle runs: cyc3vr p036, p066, p067
  - 2 push-out runs: push p036 and pushG p052
  - 2 mu03 runs from the h19 queue: p093, p145
  - 1 ASTM run: p064 compression
- **Queues:**
  - **h19:** 0 waiting, 2 running, 2624 done, 2 failed. 6 runs finished in the last 3 h, none since 13:27.
  - **evo:** empty; the 5 failed tasks are old gate2 ones.
  - **h51 drivers:** biocage_mu03G (2 windows) and biocage_mu03b (18 windows) are waiting for CPU. They count 42 busy threads, and starting one more 6-thread run would exceed the 32-core quota. No hold is blocking them.
- **Health:** nothing is dead, hung or looping. All 18 tmux sessions are up and `resume_all.sh` covers the hand-started batches. I did not do a full dry-run of `resume_all.sh` this hour, because running it would launch jobs; I checked the guards and skip rules by reading them. A restart would not re-run the failed ASTM test, because the batch skips finished tests, failed ones included.

**Needs a person:** the ASTM p064 shear45 test ended "NOT normal" after 2108 s: 104 negative jacobians, failed to converge at t=0.745. The compression test is now at t=0.742, close to the same point. A scientist should decide whether the ASTM set-up needs a change; I logged it as a problem and a request rather than restarting it.

I also logged a request for later: test fewer threads per run, or `OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive`, on new launches only, to see whether it gives more steps per hour under the throttling.

Files are in `work/agents/foreman/`:
- report_20261119_1400.md
- status.json
